name: Iʿrāb al-Qurʾān
author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
authorArabic: أبو جعفر أحمد بن محمد النحاس
about: The earliest whole iʿrāb of the Qurʾān to survive: the parsing of the hard places, with the grammarians of Baṣra and Kūfa set against each other and the readings that bear on it.

name: al-Durr al-maṣūn
titleArabic: الدر المصون في علوم الكتاب المكنون
author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
about: The fullest of the classical grammars of the Qurʾān: every way a phrase can be parsed, numbered, with who held it and the readings each depends on.

name: al-Jadwal fī iʿrāb al-Qurʾān
nameEnglish: The Table of the Qurʾān's Grammar
titleArabic: الجدول في إعراب القرآن وصرفه وبيانه
author: Maḥmūd ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥīm Ṣāfī
about: Every word of the Qurʾān parsed in order, then every sentence and its place, then the forms and their patterns, then the rhetoric — on the reading of Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim alone.

name: Iʿrāb al-Qurʾān wa-bayānuh
nameEnglish: The Grammar and Rhetoric of the Qurʾān
author: Muḥyī al-Dīn Darwīsh
about: Each passage taken in four parts — its words, its grammar, its rhetoric and what can be drawn from it — with the poetry the words are attested in.

name: Iʿrāb al-Qurʾān al-Karīm
nameEnglish: The Grammar of the Noble Qurʾān
author: Aḥmad ʿUbayd al-Daʿʿās, Aḥmad Ḥamīdān and Ismāʿīl al-Qāsim
authorArabic: أحمد عبيد الدعاس وأحمد محمد حميدان وإسماعيل محمود القاسم
credit: Aḥmad ʿUbayd al-Daʿʿās, Aḥmad Ḥamīdān and Ismāʿīl al-Qāsim
about: The shortest whole iʿrāb: each word or phrase of the ayah in its brackets, then its office in as few words as will carry it.

name: al-Iʿrāb al-muyassar
author: the compilers of al-Iʿrāb al-muyassar
about: A plain iʿrāb set out phrase by phrase, each phrase of the ayah on a line of its own with its office beside it.

name: al-Mujtabā min mushkil iʿrāb al-Qurʾān
nameEnglish: The Hard Places of the Qurʾān's Grammar
author: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad al-Kharrāṭ
about: Only the places whose grammar is hard to see, or seems at first to break the grammarians' rules: what each is, and why it holds.

name: Mafātīḥ al-aghānī
nameEnglish: The Keys to the Riches of the Readings
author: Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Kirmānī
authorArabic: أبو العلاء محمد بن أبي المحاسن الكرماني
about: The seven readers' readings, and what each reading means: the case made for every one of them.

name: al-Nashr fī al-qirāʾāt al-ʿashr
nameEnglish: The Spreading of the Ten Readings
author: Muḥammad ibn al-Jazarī
about: The reference work of the ten readings: where each of the ten readers and their transmitters reads a word otherwise, by the routes he verified.

name: Taḥbīr al-taysīr fī al-qirāʾāt al-ʿashr
author: Muḥammad ibn al-Jazarī
about: Al-Dānī's al-Taysīr on the seven readers, with Ibn al-Jazarī's addition of the three that complete the ten — the short book of the readings.

name: al-Qirāʾāt — al-Mawsūʿa al-Qurʾāniyya
nameEnglish: The Readings, from the Qurʾānic Encyclopaedia
author: Ibrāhīm ibn Ismāʿīl al-Abyārī
field: Qirāʾāt, the ten and the rest
about: Every word of the ayah read in more than one way, with each way and who read it — the readings that are not among the ten as well as those that are.
